title: THE ROLE OF SPEAKING CLUBS IN THE FORMATION OF COMMUNICATIVE COMPETENCE OF STUDENTS OF AGRICULTURAL UNIVERSITIES
extended_summary:
This paper examines the role of language clubs as an innovative extracurricular format for developing foreign-language communicative competence among students in non-language majors, especially agricultural specialities. The central problem is that conventional foreign-language instruction does not always provide enough authentic speaking practice, motivation, or intercultural engagement for future agricultural professionals.

The paper argues for language clubs (Sprachklubs) as a flexible intervention that creates a low-anxiety, informal environment for communication. It describes common formats such as thematic meetings, role plays, free conversation, games, film clubs, book clubs, debates, tandems, and mini-lessons, and then adapts these to the agricultural university context through discipline-related discussion evenings, culinary workshops, film discussions, role-play simulations of agrarian forums, project work, and meetings with native speakers. The article also highlights CLIL (Content and Language Integrated Learning) as a useful framework for combining subject content with language practice.

The population discussed is undergraduate students at a Ukrainian agricultural university, with examples drawn from students at Sumy National Agrarian University and specifically a food technologies faculty scenario. The paper concludes that language clubs can strengthen motivation, reduce speaking anxiety, support intercultural communication, and build professional terminology and oral communication skills. It also notes that online/digital language clubs are increasingly important because of COVID-19 and wartime disruptions, although the paper remains primarily conceptual and practice-oriented rather than empirical.
quality_tier_rationale: This is a conceptual/theoretical discussion paper rather than an empirical study. It does not report a controlled design, sample, or quantitative outcomes for AI use in writing instruction.
impact_tier_rationale: The paper identifies potentially meaningful pedagogical effects of AI writing tools, but it provides no measured effect sizes or direct evidence of impact. Its practical relevance is clear, but the magnitude of impact remains unclear from the evidence presented.

interventions.use_case: Use of generative AI tools such as ChatGPT and other AI-based writing assistants to support university students’ English writing through idea generation, grammar/style correction, text refinement, and feedback on drafts.

finding.finding_summary: The paper argues that AI-driven writing tools can improve the efficiency and polish of student writing by supporting idea generation, contextual prompting, grammar correction, and style refinement. At the same time, it warns that such tools may reduce authenticity, individuality, and creativity in written texts, especially when students over-rely on generated content. No original sample, effect size, or quantitative outcome data are reported.
finding.measure: Narrative assessment of writing quality, creativity, authenticity, and revision support in AI-assisted English writing
